title: Domination and hyperimmune degrees

summary: Compare computable bounds with oracle-computed functions, characterize hyperimmune degrees by their sets, and show that hyperimmune-free oracles turn Turing reductions into truth tables.
abstract: A program with an oracle can compute numerical functions that no ordinary program computes. Can their values still be bounded by ordinary computable functions? An oracle has hyperimmune degree when it computes a function that escapes every such bound, and is hyperimmune-free when each of its total numerical computations has a computable bound. We relate this distinction to infinite sets through their increasing enumerations, and construct a hyperimmune set in exactly the same degree as any oracle witnessing the first alternative. Every noncomputable set computable from the halting problem has hyperimmune degree, as a search for a first correct approximation prefix shows. Hyperimmune-freeness has a different computational consequence: every set computed from such an oracle is computed by a finite truth table, because its successful computation resources have a computable bound.
